en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-puṣpakūṭa-dhāraṇī-mantra-sūtra*, translated by the lay practitioner Zhi Qian of the Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling in the palace of the Dragon King Anavatapta at Lake Anavatapta, together with...
There were five hundred great bhikṣus together with them,
as well as one thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
all of whom had attained every dhāraṇī.
With one remaining birth, they abide in the tenth stage;
next, they shall become Buddhas,
like the crown prince of a king.
All shall simultaneously attain the Buddha-way throughout the ten directions;
possessing great adornments, they will have no doubt regarding the Tathāgata’s all-encompassing merits.
The eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, will all assemble at once.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrama rose from his seat,
knelt with his right knee on the ground,
joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, if a son or daughter of good family were to cultivate offerings toward the Tathāgata, would their merit be great?
The Buddha told Siṃhavikrama, “Do not speak such words.”
If a son or daughter of good family were to cultivate offerings to the Tathāgata,
would their merit be great? Why is this?
The Tathāgata is accomplished through immeasurable morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
If a son or daughter of good family practices offerings toward the Tathāgata,
whether he is present or has passed away, [they shall obtain great merit].
Sīhavega, you should know that such a person will ultimately attain liberation within one of the three vehicles,
according to their causes and conditions.
Furthermore, Sīhavega:
Furthermore, if there is a person who, upon seeing the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
gives rise to a heart of joy and respectfully praises him,
and offers various kinds of offerings to the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, if there are people who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata,
see his relics and give rise to a heart of joy,
these two merits are equal and without distinction.
Furthermore, Siṃhavikrama,
if a lay bodhisattva were to pile up various precious jewels as high as Mount Sumeru and offer them to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
It is not as good as a renunciant bodhisattva who, having resolved upon bodhicitta,
makes an offering of a single coin to the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, Siṃhavikrama, suppose there were another person...
If one were to attend upon the World-Honored One for ten million years, providing every form of worship and service;
yet if another person, after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, should give rise to the bodhicitta and enter a saṃghārāma with even a single incense offering or flower— [the latter would be far superior].
Lifting and lowering his feet, he spoke these words:
"Homage to the World-Honored One.
By means of this profound understanding and earnest, reverent faith, he paid homage.
They make offerings to the precious stūpas containing the relics of the Tathāgata,
neither seeking a reward nor harboring doubt,
until they attain liberation in the interim.
If, for ten million billion kalpas, one does not fall into the evil realms—
listen attentively, Siṃhavikrānta!—
there is a dhāraṇī named Puṣpasaṃcaya.
I shall now speak for the great benefit of the devas and humans.
If there is a son of good family...
If one can receive, uphold, read, recite, draw near to, and practice in accordance with the Huaji (Flower Accumulation) Dhāraṇī mantra,
their merit will surpass that [of the former].
From lifetime to lifetime, this person shall attain the power of hearing and retaining [the Dharma].
They shall not fall into the various evil paths of peril and thorns, but shall remain free from all hardships.
They shall constantly behold wondrous jewels, constantly behold all Buddhas, and their faculties shall always be complete.
They shall not be born into lowly or servile families;
they shall always remain inseparable from the bodhisattva’s expansive resolve;
and they shall always possess various kinds of immeasurable wisdom and eloquence.
Known and seen by the immeasurable Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
he then spoke this mantra:
*Taṭa* (1), *duroṇi* (2), *taroṇi* (3), *taroni* (4), *taṭa*.
1. Loni, 2. Muni, 3. Parava-sade, 4. Siddhe, 5. Candre, 6.
Namuci, 7. Kṣaṇahare, 8. Rukkhapade, 9. Buddhapade, 10. Tīre, 11. Kālajite.
Pañca-lambhā-ga-jñati 16. Jñati-du-bha-ti 17.
Viśrā-buddhi 18. Dharma-pakṣe 19. Akṣaya-karpi 20.
Kappa-viga-jñati 21. Amṛta-kappa-hūda-tātā-ni.
22. Jāpati; 23. Takkamiśa; 24. Khiciti; 25. Śukarabati; 26.
Cchanda-buddhe-dhṛti-buddhi-svāhā. Lion-like majesty, you should know this.
If a son of good family can read or recite this Flower Accumulation Divine Mantra,
that person shall, during the third, fourth, or ninth month, [attain...]
From the eighth day to the fifteenth day,
one should single-mindedly recollect the marks and signs of the Tathāgata,
and recite the Flower Accumulation Divine Mantra three times during the night.
At midday there are likewise three [offerings].
When the moon is full,
one should perform offerings before the image with incense, flowers, lamps, and candles.
He also recited the Flower Accumulation Dhāraṇī.
That night, the man dreamed of the Tathāgata,
endowed with all the marks and signs of perfection, sitting upon a lotus throne and preaching the Dharma for the assembly.
They shall also obtain the Puṣpasaṃcaya Dhāraṇī-mantra;
in this present life, they will constantly possess strong memory,
wisdom, and deep faith.
From this present life until reaching nirvana,
may they always hear and retain everything they hear and see—
every scriptural teaching and every point of study and understanding.
He attained unimpeded mastery in all arts and crafts,
achieved profound purity in all samādhis,
and realized the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma of the Four Noble Truths.
When this sutra had been spoken,
the eight classes of beings, including the devas and nāgas such as Siṃhavikrama and others,
along with the entire great assembly, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra of the Flower Accumulation Dharani Divine Incantation.
